title: Money
purpose: Every site, worker, staff member, and partner is paid on the same accepted hours that the client pays for. There is a record behind every payment. Two names go on every large payment.
how: One number runs the whole chain. The client pays the US company for accepted hours. The client pays on net 30. That means the client pays 30 days after the invoice. The US company buys the data from KMSC. KMSC pays the sites, the workers, the staff, and the partners. Every step in the chain is paid on the same hours. These are the hours the client accepted after the month-end audit. Nobody in the chain is paid for an hour the client did not accept.

Accepted means kept. A reviewer watches every video before the client sees it. The verdict is keep, flag, or delete. Kept hours are paid. Flagged footage is deleted. It is never invoiced and never paid. The wearer log shows which person made each flagged video. The handbook sets the penalty. An operator pays 100 EGP for each fraudulent video. A Portfolio Manager pays 200 EGP. If the account is banned, or the fraud is systemic, an operator pays 250 EGP and a Portfolio Manager pays 500 EGP. A flag costs the site money. That is why it is better to catch a flag early.

Mano owns the money. Mano handles payroll, site and worker payments, partner payments, reimbursements, bonuses and referrals, and the daily and monthly numbers. All money questions go to Mano. Workers ask through their Portfolio Manager. Portfolio Managers and partners ask Mano directly. Every payment is prepared against a record. The record can be the wearer log, the QC verdicts, the site or partner agreement, or the offer letter. If there is no record, there is no payment.

breaks.what: The client rejects hours we invoiced
breaks.do: Adham handles the conversation with the client. Nobody else talks to the client. Youssef Medhat matches the rejected sessions against our verdicts the same day. Any hours the client does not accept are also taken out of what we pay the sites, workers, staff, and partners. That is what it means to be paid net of fraud flags.

breaks.what: A worker says their pay is wrong
breaks.do: This goes to Mano. Mano answers within 2 working days. Bring the worker's name and role, the month, the amount they expected, and the amount they received. Mano checks the wearer log and the verdicts. If the worker disputes a flag, the flag goes to Youssef Medhat. If he reverses the flag, the pay is corrected.

breaks.what: A large payment is ready and Adham has not signed
breaks.do: The payment waits. Adham reads the number every evening, Egypt time, and the sync happens every day. So the wait is hours, not weeks. A late payment can be explained. A wrong payment cannot be taken back.

breaks.what: Someone asks Mano to move money without a record
breaks.do: The answer is no. Every payment has a record: who is paid, what the payment is for, and which hours or which agreement it is based on. Mano says no once and tells Adham the same day. If someone puts pressure on the person who holds the money, that is a problem for the founders to handle, not for Mano.

Moharam checks the facts. Mano handles the money. Adham handles the contract. All of this happens the same day. The record is the QC verdicts and the wearer log. The payment waits while any device count is open.

questions.a: At month end, through Mano. You are paid on your accepted hours, with the flagged hours taken out. You are not paid before the audit.

questions.q: Why is my pay less than my hours?
questions.a: Because of flags, or because of a penalty from the handbook table. Ask Mano. Tell Mano the month, the amount you expected, and the amount you received. If you disagree with a flag, Youssef Medhat decides on it.

questions.q: Can I know what someone else is paid?
questions.a: No. Individual pay is written in offer letters. The rules that apply to everyone are on this page.

questions.q: Who sets the threshold, and what is it?
questions.a: Adham sets it. It is not published. If Mano says a payment needs a second signature, the rule is working. It is not a delay.

principle: Every site, worker, staff member, and partner is paid on accepted hours, with the fraud flags taken out. The company is paid the same way.

approval.rule: Any payment above the approval threshold needs a second signature from Adham before the money moves.
approval.note: Two names go on every large payment. Nobody can ask Mano to move a large sum alone. Nobody can blame Mano alone.

monthEnd.text: In the last week of the month. Every audit pass is finished before any hour is totaled.
Flagged footage is deleted. It is never sent, never invoiced, and never paid.
The invoice counts accepted hours only. It does not go out before the audit is done.
Payroll, site payments, partner payments, and referral and performance bonuses. If a payment is above the threshold, Adham signs second.
